Chapter 7: Rebuilding Relationships and Finding New Family
Leaving the FLDS isn’t just about stepping away from a place—it means letting go of the people who once felt like your whole world. That kind of loss cuts deep, and the pain can stick around for a long time. Family members who stay behind often go silent, convinced you’re gone for good. That silence? It’s heavy, filled with longing and questions that never seem to get answered.
At first, the loneliness can be almost unbearable. Holidays and birthdays come and go quietly, and you can’t help but remember those crowded tables, the laughter you once shared. The ache for siblings, parents, and childhood friends becomes this constant shadow. It’s wild how much our sense of who we are is wrapped up in family—those little rituals and routines that once felt like they’d last forever.
But here’s where things start to shift. In that emptiness, something new begins to grow. Maybe it’s a neighbor who invites you over for dinner. Or a coworker who turns into someone you can really talk to. Support groups—where everyone’s carrying a bit of the same pain and hope—can turn strangers into something like family. It’s not about blood or tradition anymore. It’s about choice, and about people showing up for each other.
Sometimes, there are even glimmers of reconciliation. Every so often, a letter might arrive from a sibling still inside the FLDS—a hesitant step, a question about what life’s like now. Those conversations feel fragile, a mix of hope and fear. Rebuilding trust isn’t quick, and not every bond will survive. But just knowing that reconnecting is possible? That offers comfort.
Learning to set boundaries is a whole new thing. For years, she was taught to put everyone else first, to just accept whatever was asked of her. Now, she’s learning how to say no—to protect her own well-being. It’s tough at first, and guilt and doubt sneak in. But with practice, setting boundaries becomes a real source of strength.
Over time, she realizes that family isn’t just about where you come from. It’s about who’s there for you when things get hard. These new relationships—built on honesty, respect, and genuine care—they prove just how powerful human connection can be, even after so much loss.
The journey of rebuilding never really ends. There are setbacks and tough days, but there are also moments that bring real joy. She learns it’s possible to honor the past while still reaching for the future—to grieve what’s gone, and celebrate what’s been found.
